conventions.convention: Arc surgery replaces two interior disks by the lateral annulus of an embedded product cylinder approaching the same cooriented side at both feet, with compatible orientation; its reverse is a reduction.

Use full AC, connected compact smooth oriented spanning surfaces, and first-variable positive push: V_ij = lk(a_i⁺,a_j). The positive normal n satisfies that (n,u,v) is ambient-positive for a positive surface frame (u,v).
H_ω = (1−ω)V + (1−ω̄)Vᵀ for ω ∈ S¹ excluding 1. Matrix signature omits zero eigenvalues; the knot invariant at an Alexander root is instead the arithmetic mean of the two nonroot one-sided limits.
The Seifert quadratic enhancement is q(x)=xᵀVx modulo two; Arf is the sum of q(a_i)q(b_i) in a symplectic basis, with empty sum zero.
Conway normalization is ∇_U=1 and ∇_+−∇_−=z∇_0 with the stated projected-tangent crossing sign. For knots, Δ#(1)=1, Δ#(t⁻¹)=Δ#(t), and z=t¹ᐟ²−t⁻¹ᐟ².

load_bearing.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let L be a nonempty smooth oriented link in the oriented 3-sphere, and let F₀,F₁ be connected compact smooth oriented embedded surfaces with the same oriented boundary L. There is a finite sequence of such spanning surfaces from F₀ to F₁ in which each consecutive pair differs either by an ambient isotopy fixed on L or by one embedded arc surgery or its reverse.

Under full AC, every nonempty smooth oriented link bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface. Θ_L(u)=det(u⁻¹V−uVᵀ) is independent of surface and integral basis, belongs to Z[u−u⁻¹], equals 1 for the unknot, and satisfies Θ_+−Θ_−=(u−u⁻¹)Θ_0.

Under full AC, positive-push Seifert matrices in arbitrary integral bases of any two connected compact smooth oriented spanning surfaces for the same smooth oriented knot are related by finitely many integral unimodular congruences and the two rank-two elementary enlargements or their reverses.

Under full AC, q_F(x)=xᵀVx modulo two is well-defined on H₁(F;F₂), has nondegenerate intersection polarization, and has basis-independent Arf sum. This sum is unchanged by either elementary Seifert enlargement and depends only on the knot.
Under full AC, for a smooth oriented knot with an integral symplectic Seifert matrix, Δ#_K(t)=1+Arf(K)(1+t)²/t in F₂[t,t⁻¹]/(1+t)⁴.

Under full AC, integral unimodular congruences and either elementary Seifert enlargement or reduction preserve the signature of H_ω for every ω ∈ S¹ excluding 1. Consequently the nonroot signature and one-sided-average values at Alexander roots are independent of surface and basis.

concerns.concern: The Definition takes an assignment P 'to each ambient-isotopy class of oriented links' and says the determinant lemma 'constructs a unique assignment'. The cited link definition allows k ∈ N components, and def-natural-numbers includes 0, so this domain includes the empty link. The determinant supplier explicitly treats only nonempty links. Neither the unknot normalization nor any crossing-ball skein triple constrains P on the empty link: two extensions agreeing on every nonempty link but assigning different integer polynomials to the empty link satisfy the same stated conditions. Thus the claimed uniqueness on the Definition's domain is false unless that domain excludes the empty link or an empty-link value is separately prescribed.

Proof 2.1 writes 'x=∑_i(a_i a_i+b_i b_i) with a_i,b_i ∈ F₂', reusing the symplectic basis-vector names as scalar coordinates. The subsequent Gauss-sum calculation is sound, but this coordinate expansion needs distinct scalar names to be well-typed.

seams_checked.note: The pairing, skew-intersection identity, isotopy congruence, and elementary enlargement conventions match their actual uses.
Uses the determinant only up to Laurent units before imposing the unique symmetric value-one normalization; the separate fraction D_K is not substituted for Δ_K.
Both displayed matrices and Alexander determinants match ex-knot-kt-07-worked-cases; symmetric normalization gives 1+z² and 1−z².
The concordance-surjection proof uses precisely the finite S-equivalence sequence for matrices of the same knot, under full AC.
The metabolizer theorem restricts to nonroot parameters, where matrix inertia equals the defined knot signature, and uses the stated surface invariance.

The zero-surgery cover splitting uses total linking as signed surface intersection under AC. The finite-cyclic defect formula explicitly uses raw character-matrix inertia, including singular forms, without identifying it with the root-averaged knot signature.
The unknotting bound uses H_−1=2(V+Vᵀ), proves nonsingularity at −1 by reduction modulo two, and then invokes surface and basis invariance.
